Citizen Lab: Discover Tech weaponized ad infrastructure for zero-click spyware ⭐️ 9.0/10

Citizen Lab research reveals that Israeli firm Discover Tech used targeted advertising infrastructure to create a delivery pipeline for zero-click mercenary spyware. The report demonstrates how ad-tech supply chains can be exploited to install surveillance software without user interaction, representing a new class of exploitation in digital advertising. The Guardian and The Verge have independently reported on the findings.

hackernews · jcomp · Oct 15, 10:43 · Discussion

「Background」 Citizen Lab's AdFection report details how Discover Tech's Controlium ad platform was used to profile targets and deliver zero-click spyware from Candiru and Bindecy to at least 45 Al Jazeera journalists' devices. The research demonstrates that real-time bidding infrastructure can be weaponized to selectively exploit victims without any user interaction, representing a new supply-chain attack vector in digital advertising.

「Impact」 The Citizen Lab findings show that ad-tech supply chains can be weaponized to deliver zero-click mercenary spyware, meaning high-value targets can be compromised simply by loading a malicious ad—no click or user interaction required. This expands the threat model for journalists, activists, and officials who previously relied on avoiding suspicious links; standard browser sandboxing and ad-blockers may not stop an exploit delivered through a legitimate ad exchange. Organizations should audit their ad-tech exposure, enforce strict Content Security Policies, and treat ad networks as potential initial-access vectors in threat modeling.

「Community discussion」 Commenters debate the novelty of the "zero-click" claim, with an ad-tech engineer arguing the report is sensationalist and vague on the actual exploit mechanism. Others discuss the concentration of mercenary spyware firms in Israel, referencing the "Download Valley" ecosystem, and question the trustworthiness of Israeli cyber companies given potential state ties.

References

Libreboot 26.10 adds UEFI support and 233 Chromebooks ⭐️ 8.0/10

Libreboot 26.10 "Ominous Olive" introduces UEFI/EDK integration and imports all 233 Chromebooks currently supported by the MrChromebox coreboot distribution, dramatically expanding hardware compatibility. The release is source-only, requiring users to build from source with no pre-built binaries provided. Baytrail (Kip) devices have been tested, while other Chromebooks need community testing.

hackernews · iamnothere · Oct 15, 12:52 · Discussion

「Background」 Libreboot is a free and open-source BIOS/UEFI boot firmware distribution based on coreboot. The MrChromebox project provides custom coreboot firmware and utilities for Chromebooks and Chromeboxes, maintaining a distro of coreboot ports for many Chrome OS devices. Libreboot 26.10 imports all 233 currently supported Chromebooks from the MrChromebox coreboot distro and adds UEFI support via EDK 2 integration.

「Impact」 The UEFI/EDK integration and Chromebook import significantly increase the number of devices that can run Libreboot and simplify future porting efforts. Users with supported Chromebooks must build the firmware from source, and most devices beyond Baytrail (Kip) remain untested in this release.

「Community discussion」 Commenters highlight the UEFI/EDK integration and Chromebook support as the major technical advance, noting it multiplies supported devices and eases future ports. One contributor relates this to ongoing Heads project work porting ChromeOS devices using MrChromebox code. Others discuss the project's new policy restricting LLM-assisted contributions, with mixed views on its merits.

References

  • Libreboot – Free and Open Source BIOS/ UEFI boot firmware

MIT: Randomly connected units self-organize learning machinery matching backprop performance ⭐️ 8.0/10

MIT News reports on a PNAS study showing that randomly interconnected neuron-like units governed by shared local plasticity rules can spontaneously self-organize functional learning motifs. These self-assembled circuits achieve pattern recognition and image classification performance comparable to networks trained with backpropagation. The research demonstrates a biologically plausible alternative to explicitly designed learning circuits, though the authors caution that self-organization does not prove the brain uses this mechanism, and stability across initial conditions and task generalization remain open questions.

reddit · r/MachineLearning · /u/Dorian182 · Oct 15, 10:01

「Background」 The PNAS paper "How Biological Synapses Self-Assemble Gradient Learning" (9 October 2026) and the accompanying MIT News report (13 October 2026) describe a study from the McGovern Institute showing that randomly interconnected neuron-like units, governed by shared local plasticity rules, can spontaneously self-organize functional learning motifs that achieve pattern-recognition and image-classification performance comparable to networks trained with backpropagation. The work is framed as a step toward biologically plausible learning mechanisms rather than a demonstrated replacement for backpropagation in large-scale models.

「Impact」 The findings advance neuromorphic computing and biologically plausible learning research by showing local plasticity rules can replace global error signals for gradient-like learning. This could inform future hardware-efficient learning systems, but practical deployment in large-scale models remains future work.

References
  • How artificial neural networks build their own learning machinery | MIT News

Tags: #neuromorphic computing, #biologically plausible learning, #self-organizing systems, #local plasticity rules, #backpropagation alternatives

Shanghai AI Lab Releases Atria Dawn 744B MoE Agent Model ⭐️ 8.0/10

Shanghai AI Laboratory released Atria Dawn on October 12, a 744-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts agent model built on the GLM-5.2 architecture with a 256K-token context window. The model is licensed under MIT, with both code and weights open-sourced, and supports local deployment as well as hosted access. Official demonstrations show capabilities in protein structure prediction, CAD modeling, knowledge visualization, slide-deck creation, and data analysis.

telegram · zaihuapd · Oct 16, 01:32

「Background」 Atria Dawn is built on GLM-5.2, a 744-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model released by Z.ai in June 2026. Shanghai AI Laboratory applied agentic post-training using a Verifiable Experience Pipeline that grounds tasks in real execution environments and verifies outcomes against external signals. The model targets long-horizon scientific and engineering workflows such as protein structure prediction, CAD modeling, and data analysis.

「Impact」 Developers and researchers can now run a 744B-parameter MoE agent model locally or via hosted access under an MIT license, with a 256K context window and demonstrated tool-use for protein structure prediction, CAD modeling, and data analysis. The Hugging Face repository confirms MIT-licensed weights and code, though the LICENSE file link currently returns a 404, so users should verify the exact license text before commercial deployment.

SemiAnalysis: AMD MI355X beats Nvidia on cost for massive MoE inference ⭐️ 8.0/10

SemiAnalysis published benchmarks using its open-source AgentX dataset — 1M+ token, multi-turn code-generation traces with 95%+ KV-cache hit rates — to test real-world agent workloads. Through 70+ open-source PRs, TileLang fused kernels (including fused MLA and FP8 KV cache), and the custom ATOM runtime, AMD's MI355X doubled throughput on frontier models such as DeepSeek-V4-Pro in 26 days. In extreme low-latency (>150 tok/s) and massive dense-model scenarios, Nvidia Blackwell still holds a 2–5× energy and cost advantage via NVLink and FP4. However, for massive MoE models (Kimi K3, GLM-5.3) and medium-latency workloads, the MI355X's 288 GB VRAM enables higher batch density, delivering 9–40% lower cost per million tokens — a localized breach of the CUDA moat.

telegram · zaihuapd · Oct 16, 02:30

「Background」 SemiAnalysis developed the AgentX benchmark, a $3M real-world agent trajectory dataset that replays 1M+ token contexts, multi-turn branching, and 95%+ KV cache hit rates for code generation workloads. The MI355X is AMD's CDNA 4 architecture GPU with 288GB HBM3E memory and 8TB/s bandwidth, marking AMD's first chip with FP4 support. Prior Horizon coverage noted SemiAnalysis reported an 11-fold performance gain for MI355X on AgentX using MiniMax M3 after 19 days of software improvements, highlighting rapid optimization via TileLang fused kernels and the ATOM runtime.

「Procurement Impact」 Organizations deploying massive MoE models such as Kimi K3 or GLM-5.3 at medium latency can achieve 9–40% lower cost per million tokens by using AMD MI355X instead of Nvidia Blackwell, because the 288 GB VRAM enables higher batch density. For ultra-low-latency interactive workloads (>150 tok/s) or very large dense models, Nvidia retains a 2–5× efficiency and cost advantage due to NVLink and FP4 support.

Meta releases Muse Spark Open 816B MoE model for local deployment ⭐️ 7.0/10

Meta has released Muse Spark Open, an 816-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 42 billion active parameters, optimized for local deployment on consumer hardware such as Mac Studio. The model weights are available on Hugging Face and Meta provides deployment guides for runtimes including MLX, Unsloth, and others. The license permits broad use but restricts Model-as-a-Service offerings when the licensee's aggregate gross revenue exceeds $20 million. Early benchmarks cited in community discussion indicate the model underperforms some contemporary open models such as Qwen3.8 Flash Next and GLM 5.3 Flash.

hackernews · bigwheels · Oct 15, 17:47 · Discussion

「Background」 Meta previously released the Llama series of open-weight models, most recently Llama 3.1 in July 2024, which established a pattern of large-scale open releases with commercial-use restrictions. Muse Spark Open follows that lineage as a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 816 billion total parameters and 42 billion active parameters, adding multimodal support for text, images, audio, and video, plus a 1-million-token context window. The model is distributed under the Muse Model License, which permits broad use but requires a separate agreement for Model-as-a-Service providers whose aggregate gross revenue exceeds $20 million in any 12-month period.

「Impact」 Developers can deploy Muse Spark Open locally on consumer hardware such as Mac Studio using runtimes including MLX and Unsloth, but the model scores 52 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0—behind Gemini 3.1 Pro, GPT-5.4, and Claude Opus 4.6—and the license restricts Model-as-a-Service use when the licensee's aggregate gross revenue exceeds $20 million.

「Community discussion」 Commenters note that artificial analysis benchmarks show Muse Spark Open underperforming Qwen3.8 Flash Next and GLM 5.3 Flash, both runnable on a single B300 GPU. The license's revenue-based restriction on Model-as-a-Service is debated as limiting openness. Meta's broad runtime support (MLX, Unsloth, etc.) is praised for deployment ease. One commenter argues Meta is building a sticky ecosystem around its models as a strategic moat.

Krea 3 launches open beta for fast, low-cost regional image editing ⭐️ 7.0/10

Krea has opened the beta of Krea 3, a new foundational image model that emphasizes native regional editing, precise edits, and high quality at lower cost and latency than prior models. The announcement comes from Krea founder Diego and references a technical report for the previous Krea 2 release, though no technical details, benchmarks, or open-weight release are available for Krea 3 yet. The model is currently accessible only through Krea's hosted service with a limited free trial followed by a monthly subscription.

hackernews · dvrp · Oct 15, 16:04 · Discussion

「Background」 Krea previously released Krea 2 with a technical report detailing its architecture and training approach. The company has established a pattern of providing substantive technical disclosures for its foundational image models, and the founder indicated a similar technical update is planned for Krea 3.

「Impact」 Designers and developers can test Krea 3's regional editing capabilities for UI and design workflows, but must use Krea's hosted platform and accept a subscription model after a two-image trial. Community members have posted direct visual comparisons with GPT-Image-2.5 showing similar quality on landing page and website design tasks, though the closed, hosted nature and lack of open weights limit local deployment and customization options.

「Community discussion」 Commenters are requesting open-weight releases to enable local inference and fine-tuning, with one noting that closed access may limit adoption compared to OpenAI and Google offerings. Several users object to the subscription-only pricing after a two-image trial, preferring credit-based models. The founder indicated an open-weight release is under consideration but not confirmed.

Fortran Turns 70: First High-Level Language Still Powers Scientific Computing ⭐️ 7.0/10

Fortran, the first high-level programming language, marks its 70th anniversary. Originally developed by John Backus and his team at IBM, Fortran pioneered concepts like compilers and high-level abstractions that shaped modern programming. Today it remains essential in high-performance computing, climate modeling, and scientific simulations, with modern standards (Fortran 2018/2023) adding features like coarrays for parallelism and improved interoperability with C.

hackernews · rbanffy · Oct 15, 15:03 · Discussion

「Background」 Fortran (FORmula TRANslation) was developed by an IBM team led by John Backus and first released in 1957 as the first high-level programming language, designed for scientific and engineering computation. The language introduced concepts such as compilers, optimization, and array-oriented syntax that shaped subsequent languages and established the foundation for modern high-performance computing. The Fortran standards committee continues to evolve the language, with Fortran 2023 being the latest major revision adding features like parallel computing constructs and improved interoperability with C.

「Impact」 Decades-old Fortran codebases — some exceeding 700,000 lines — remain in active maintenance and production use, particularly in simulation solvers and numerical libraries. Developers working in scientific computing still choose modern Fortran for linear algebra and numerical workloads due to its performance and native array semantics, which can be more expressive than C for these domains.

「Community Discussion」 Hacker News commenters shared firsthand experiences maintaining legacy Fortran systems, including removing Hollerith string encodings and working with the Dynosour dynamic memory system based on equivalenced arrays. One developer noted writing Fortran in 2018 for simulation solvers and preferring it over C for linear algebra. The Computer History Museum's oral history of John Backus was highlighted as a valuable resource for understanding the language's origins.

ASML Reportedly Developing Hybrid Bonding Tool for Advanced Packaging ⭐️ 7.0/10

ASML appears to be developing a hybrid bonding tool based on patent filings, a news report, and its public roadmap, though the company has not made an official announcement. Hybrid bonding is a critical technology for 3D stacking, chiplet integration, and high-bandwidth memory production. ASML's potential entry would expand its portfolio beyond EUV lithography into advanced packaging equipment.

rss · Semianalysis · Oct 15, 19:27

「Background」 Hybrid bonding is a wafer-level interconnect technology that enables direct copper-to-copper and dielectric-to-dielectric bonds without solder bumps, allowing sub-micron pitch connections critical for 3D stacking, chiplet integration, and high-bandwidth memory. ASML currently dominates extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography for front-end wafer fabrication but has not previously supplied advanced packaging equipment; established players in hybrid bonding include BE Semiconductor Industries (Besi) and EV Group.

「Impact」 ASML's potential entry into hybrid bonding equipment would introduce a major new competitor in a market projected to grow from $200 million in 2025 to $931 million by 2033 at a 21.2% CAGR, potentially accelerating tool availability and cost reductions for chipmakers adopting 3D stacking and chiplet architectures.

Google Launches New AI-Powered Android Scam Protections ⭐️ 7.0/10

Google announced new AI-driven Android scam protections rolling out across Messages, Chrome, WebView, and call handling. Google Messages gains an enhanced protection mode that uses cloud-based Gemini for deep scam-intent analysis of unknown conversations and on-device Gemini Nano for real-time link safety checks. Screen-sharing masking for passwords and payment pages now extends to Chrome and WebView components. The system also adds background interception of call forwarding and manual-entry warnings to prevent one-time password theft.

telegram · zaihuapd · Oct 15, 12:39

「Background」 Google has been progressively integrating its Gemini AI models into Android security features. Earlier reporting noted that Chrome and Android WebView would begin hiding login fields and payment interfaces during screen sharing, with a planned October rollout on Android 15 and later devices.

「Impact」 Android users gain stronger, automated defenses against phishing links, social-engineering scams in messaging, and OTP interception via call forwarding, without needing to change behavior. Developers using WebView inherit the screen-sharing masking for sensitive pages automatically.

Tesla Unveils SpaceX Thruster-Equipped Roadster Targeting 2028 Production ⭐️ 7.0/10

The prototype demonstrated extreme maneuvers including driving up an inverted ramp, rotating mid-air, and jumping over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, and Model Y, achieving a claimed 0-60 mph time of roughly one second. Elon Musk stated production is targeted for 2028; pricing was not disclosed, though reservations require a $50,000 deposit and a top-tier "Rocket" variant is invitation-only. All three range variants are rated at 300 miles with a top speed exceeding 230 mph.

telegram · zaihuapd · Oct 16, 02:02

The vehicle has faced repeated delays, with production originally targeted for 2021, then 2023, and later 2024. The current 2028 production target and the Waco demonstration represent the first public showing of the thruster system integrated into a prototype vehicle.

However, the 2028 production target and absence of final specifications or pricing mean developers and buyers have no actionable compatibility or purchasing information at this stage.

Scaling Kimi K3 on AMD MI355X: Matching NVIDIA B300 Throughput ⭐️ 8.0/10

rss · vLLM Blog · Oct 16, 00:00

「Background」 AMD and vLLM collaborators optimized Kimi K3 inference on an eight-GPU AMD Instinct MI355X system to match and exceed NVIDIA HGX B300 throughput per GPU on the AgentX benchmark, which replays real coding-agent session traces with over 96% theoretical prefix reuse. At 50 tokens/s/user P90 interactivity, MI355X delivers 7,567 total tokens/s/GPU versus 6,083 for B300 (24.4% advantage), translating to 87.4% more tokens per dollar under SemiAnalysis's modeled TCO ($1.50 vs $2.26 per GPU-hour). Both GPUs share 288 GB HBM3E and 8 TB/s peak bandwidth, though B300 has higher dense matrix peaks (13.5 PFLOP/s FP4 vs 10.1 PFLOP/s MXFP4).

「Solution」 The optimization spans six areas. (1) Decode Context Parallelism (DCP8) splits MLA's compressed KV history across GPUs, reducing per-GPU cache from ~1.96 GB to ~245 MB for a 142K-token conversation, while CPU offload preserves reusable state in host DRAM with aligned MLA/KDA resume points. (2) MoE output projection deduplication assigns each GPU only its output coordinates, reusing the existing shared-expert all-reduce to assemble full results without new collectives, yielding 3–5% throughput gains and freeing ~3.85 GiB/GPU for more cached state (28.9% gain at high concurrency where cache hit rate rose from 74.8% to 80.1%). (3) Kernel fusion eliminates redundant copies: KDA single-token decode fused three kernels and two copies into one launch (AttnRes fusion gave 14.2% throughput gain), and the GEMM dispatcher stopped packing inputs for unused fallback paths (removing 69 copies/step, saving 0.339 ms/step). (4) MLA long-context decoding accelerated by padding 12 query heads to 16 to unlock AMD AITER's assembly path, halving time per output token from 43.8 ms to 23.6 ms at 32K input length. (5) KDA parallelization uses fused prefill with group summaries to break sequential dependencies, and speculative verification switched to 4-column tiles (384 workgroups vs 48), cutting per-layer verification from 16.2 µs to 5.61 µs (2.89×). (6) Speculative decoding draft depth is tuned by cost budget: four drafts give 12% more committed tokens per cycle but only help if the full cycle takes <12% longer than three drafts; the recipe uses 3–7 drafts with DCP1 and disables speculation at DCP8.

「Takeaway」 Sustained software engineering across the vLLM stack—cache parallelism, MoE deduplication, kernel fusion, attention scheduling, recurrent state parallelization, and speculative decoding tradeoffs—enabled AMD MI355X to match NVIDIA B300 throughput per GPU and exceed it per dollar on a realistic agent workload, demonstrating that inference optimization requires coordinating serving decisions with kernel-level hardware utilization rather than relying on peak FLOPs alone.

IMF: Rural Chinese households spend 8.7% of income on healthcare, nearly matching U.S. share despite far lower incomes ⭐️ 7.0/10

IMF research shows rural Chinese households spend 8.7% of disposable income on healthcare — second only to the U.S. at 9.9% — even though U.S. per capita disposable income ($68,289) is over ten times China's ($6,400). The IMF says this burden drives high savings and weak consumption, and recommends higher government health and social spending, especially in rural areas.

rss · CNBC Finance · Oct 15, 23:00

「Background」 The findings come from an IMF book titled "Toward a New Economic Growth Model for China," which outlines structural reforms to shift China's economy from investment-led growth toward stronger household consumption.

「Impact」 High out-of-pocket healthcare costs push rural and migrant households to save more and spend less, weighing on China's shift to consumption-led growth; the IMF estimates targeted rural health and social spending could meaningfully lower the rural savings rate.

References
  • Front Matter in: Toward a New Economic Growth Model for China

Tags: #China, #healthcare costs, #household savings, #IMF, #consumption

China says rare earth exports to EU will continue regardless of U.S. trade deal ⭐️ 7.0/10

China's Commerce Ministry said it will keep approving rare earth export licenses to Europe even if the U.S.-China trade truce expires in January, easing supply-chain concerns for EU manufacturers.

rss · CNBC Finance · Oct 15, 09:02

「Background」 China imposed sweeping rare earth export controls in October 2025 after the U.S. expanded its entity list to cover thousands of Chinese firms, but the U.S. and China agreed to a one-year suspension at a summit in Busan that October, later extended by two months to January 2026. EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič met Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao in early October 2026, and China offered a "green channel" to keep rare earths flowing to Europe while seeking EU support for Chinese imports in dual-use sectors.

「Impact」 European automotive, electronics, and defense industries that rely on Chinese rare earths gain more supply certainty, reducing the risk of disruption if U.S.-China tensions resume.
